source_text: Si ante peccatum per Deum creatum est unde homines nascerentur, per diabolum autem unde parentes commoverentur, adscribetur sine dubio sanctitas nascentibus et culpa generantibus. Quod quia manifestissime nuptias damnat, amoveto hunc sensum precor de ecclesiarum medio et vere credito quia per Iesum Christum ìàcta sunt omnia et sine ipso factum est nihil
pass_a_gloss: If before sin it was created through God from which human beings would be born, but through the devil that from which parents would be moved, holiness will without doubt be ascribed to those being born and guilt to those begetting. Because this most manifestly condemns marriages, remove this sense, I pray, from the midst of the churches, and truly believe that through Jesus Christ all things were made and without him nothing was made.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: If, before sin, God created what human beings would be born from, but the devil supplied what would arouse their parents, holiness will undoubtedly be assigned to the newborn and guilt to those who beget them. Since this most clearly condemns marriage, please remove this view from the churches’ midst. Truly believe that through Jesus Christ all things were made, and without him nothing was made (John 1:3).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
